guide.summary: Use OpenProject's documented OAuth2 authorization code flow with the api_v3 scope to read work package titles through GET /api/v3/work_packages, paged with offset and pageSize. Start on a developer-owned test instance: register an OAuth application, implement the callback and token exchange, authorize a representative test user, then run paged read checks. Production needs a customer administrator to create the application on each customer instance. Supplied sources do not document provider review, cross-instance registration, or a read-only scope, so those stay open.

findings.title: OpenProject documents an OAuth2 authorization code flow for API access
findings.detail: The OAuth endpoints and the authorization code exchange are documented, so the connected person can authorize the app against their own instance. Client credentials is not the right fit for this access.

findings.title: Request the api_v3 scope for the standard API
findings.detail: api_v3 is documented as the standard OpenProject API scope and is the default when no scope is checked. It is the mapped grant for reading work packages. The documents do not describe a read-only variant, so the no-modify rule must be enforced in the app.

findings.title: Use the authorization code flow, not client credentials, for connected-person access
findings.detail: Client credentials requires an application bound to an impersonating user for non-public access. Connected-person reads should use the user's own authorization.

steps.detail: Sign in as the test user on the test instance, approve consent, and let the callback exchange the code. Record the access token and expires_in for the next checks. Do not use an administrator account.
steps.doneWhen: The token response includes an access_token and an expires_in value for the test user.

steps.title: Read work package titles, first page (read-work-package-titles)
steps.detail: Call the list endpoint with filters set to an empty array and pageSize 5. Expected: a HAL+JSON collection of work packages with title values. Boundary check: confirm only work packages visible to the test user appear. Confirm the outgoing request log shows only this GET. Do not send any write request to test the boundary.
steps.doneWhen: The first page returns titles for visible work packages and the request log shows only GET.

evidence.quote: get /api/v3/work_packages Returns a collection of work packages.
Parameters offset integer optional query
optional query JSON specifying filter conditions. Accepts the same format as returned by the queries endpoint. If no filter is to be applied, the client should send an empty array

steps.title: Read work package titles, second page (read-work-package-titles)
steps.detail: Repeat the list call with offset 2 and pageSize 5. Expected: a second page that does not repeat items from page one. Boundary check: compare page one and page two IDs and confirm only GET requests appear in the log.
steps.doneWhen: Page two returns different work packages from page one and the request log shows only GET.

evidence.quote: Parameters offset integer optional query
Page number inside the requested collection.
Number of elements to display per page.

steps.detail: Each customer administrator creates the application on their own instance and shares the client ID and secret through a secure channel. Launch is blocked until this is complete for each instance.
steps.doneWhen: Each target customer instance lists the OAuth application and the connected person can complete authorization.
